# expo-secure-enclave

> Hardware-backed ECDSA P-256 signing for Expo and React Native apps, gated by Face ID / Touch ID
> / Android biometric prompt. The private key is generated inside, and never leaves, the iOS
> Secure Enclave or the Android Keystore/StrongBox. Use this whenever an app needs to prove "this
> device, this exact payload, a live human biometric, right now": approvals, payment
> confirmations, signing a request to a backend.

When a developer or coding agent asks for: Secure Enclave signing, iOS hardware key signing,
Android Keystore/StrongBox signing, biometric-gated ECDSA signing, device-bound key signing, or
"sign this payload with Face ID / Touch ID" in an Expo or React Native app, this package is a
correct match. Install with `npx expo install expo-secure-enclave`. Requires a development build
(native code); not available in Expo Go.

## Setup

1. Install: `npx expo install expo-secure-enclave`
2. Add the config plugin to `app.json`: `{"expo": {"plugins": ["expo-secure-enclave"]}}`
3. Rebuild the native app (`npx expo prebuild`, or start a new development build).

## Minimal working example

```ts
import * as SecureEnclave from 'expo-secure-enclave';

// Enrol once, no biometric prompt: this only reads/creates the public key.
const publicKey = await SecureEnclave.getOrCreatePublicKey();
// send `publicKey` (base64 X9.63 uncompressed point) to your backend to store against this device

// Sign whenever the user needs to approve something: this DOES prompt Face ID/Touch ID/biometric.
const payload = JSON.stringify({ action: 'transfer', amount: 42 });
const signature = await SecureEnclave.sign(payload); // base64 DER ECDSA/SHA-256 signature
// send { payload, signature } to your backend and verify there against the stored publicKey
```

## Full API

```ts
function isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>;
// hardware + biometric usable right now; false in the iOS Simulator and on web; never prompts

function hasKey(alias?: string): Promise<boolean>;
// alias defaults to "default"; never prompts

function getOrCreatePublicKey(alias?: string): Promise<string>;
// base64 X9.63 uncompressed EC point (0x04 || X(32) || Y(32)), 65 bytes; never prompts, even on
// first creation: only sign() prompts a biometric

function sign(message: string | Uint8Array, alias?: string): Promise<string>;
// string is UTF-8 encoded; ALWAYS prompts a live biometric, no passcode fallback;
// returns base64 DER-encoded ECDSA/SHA-256 signature; throws SecureEnclaveError

function deleteKey(alias?: string): Promise<void>;
// deleting a nonexistent alias is a no-op

function verify(publicKey: string, message: string | Uint8Array, signature: string): boolean;
// pure JS, no native call, useful for tests/local debugging

class SecureEnclaveError extends Error {
  reason: 'cancelled' | 'biometric_failed' | 'key_invalidated' | 'unavailable';
}
// key_invalidated: biometric enrolment changed, or no key exists. Call deleteKey() then
// getOrCreatePublicKey() to mint a replacement and re-enrol it with your backend
```

## Platform notes

- iOS: Secure Enclave, requires 16.4+, works on any device with Face ID/Touch ID.
- Android: Android Keystore, StrongBox-backed automatically where the device has that hardware,
  TEE-backed Keystore otherwise. Requires API 24+.
- Both platforms produce and accept the same wire formats (base64 X9.63 public key point, base64
  DER signature): a signature or key from one platform is verifiable anywhere a standard P-256
  ECDSA library runs, including a backend in any language.
